Cross-check = master: voluntary_return_status=yes over in_headline=1 (includes insider and MEV-bot returns, mixed cases). numbers.question: What is the typical bounty / split?
numbers.canonical_value: 10% is the price: median opening offer 10% in every year since 2021 (102 of 181 openings dated 2020 or later are exactly 10%); attackers who settle keep the offered share (median 10%, n=35; exactly the offer in 21). Recent public negotiated returns retained a median 3.0% (n=10, range 0% to 25%).
numbers.definition: Opening bounty = percentage offered in the team's first on-chain message (181 recorded openings dated 2020 or later in the shipped by-year table; its 2020 median is 12.145%, so the yearly 10% median applies from 2021). The earlier 104 of 183 pooled count adds two 2017 Parity-coded records from the prior study, one without a source URL; those records are not shipped and are excluded from this opening-offer denominator. Kept = share of the loss the attacker finally kept in 35 incidents with both an opening and a recorded retention. Settlement-split sample = 10 recent negotiated returns with a stated returned share (Poly, Euler, Munchables, Thala, KiloEx, GMX, Verus, Renegade, NEAR Intents, 79thVault), returned share of loss, Liquid and Mango excluded. Poly Network has 100% recorded recovery across ~$578M voluntary and ~$33M frozen; its voluntary share is 94.6% and its retained share is zero. The retained-share calculation includes assets frozen outside the attacker's control. Euler's post-mortem reports full recovery.

numbers.question: Does messaging matter?
numbers.canonical_value: Messaging is strongly associated with a return but not shown to cause one. Teams that reached out saw a return in 36.5% of known cases vs 3.5% without outreach (80 of 219 vs 9 of 256); outreach roughly doubled 2020-2026 while the return rate stayed 14-22%; no measurable association was detected for the tested terms (offer size, deadline, legal threat, non-pursuit promise, tone), in underpowered observational tests.
numbers.definition: Known-outcome cases only, frame of 1,078 large exploits/key compromises (see R1). Association is non-causal: teams reach out when the attacker already looks willing. Strongest correlate: attacker reply (65 of 79 repliers returned vs 3 of 100 silent; coded in the same review pass as the return). Reply measure independent of the outcome (chain-scan attacker-class message): 6 of 7 vs 50 of 143. Tests on tactics are underpowered (minimum detectable odds ratio 3.3-4.4).

numbers.question: Has any real exploit been verifiably written or found by AI?
numbers.canonical_value: No verified case. We found no post-mortem, security-firm statement, PoC comment or verified attacker-contract source that attributes an in-the-wild exploit to an AI model. Of 28 AI-related claims logged (data/ai_incident_claims.csv): 12 verified (mostly lab results, tool use in malware, social engineering or defender-side), 10 credible-claim, 6 speculation. Speculation is flagged, not findings: TRM via Bloomberg on the two April 2026 heists, reported as Drift and Kelp ("highly likely" AI-assisted, no evidence offered), Chainalysis on unverified contracts (no incident attributed to AI), the Immunefi and OpenZeppelin-alumni opinion pieces. numbers.question: What do the AI exploit benchmarks actually show?
numbers.canonical_value: Benchmarks measure simulated exploit capability. SCONE-bench (Anthropic, 1 Dec 2025): 10 models produced working exploits for 207 of 405 historical contracts (51.11%, best of 8 attempts), $550.1M of simulated value; on post-cutoff contracts $4.6M; zero-day run on 2,849 contracts found 2 novel bugs ($3,694 simulated, API cost $3,476). reconciliations.topic: Any-channel recovery 19.0% vs voluntary ~8-10% vs non-voluntary 6.6%/3.5%
reconciliations.explanation: Three different numerators over three different denominators. 19.0% = every documented recovery channel (theft-date USD except Liquid (press-reported USD), capped, make-whole excluded) over all $16.52B of headline losses. Voluntary = attacker/insider return only: 10.0% on the same denominator; 8.2% in the prior paper (571 known-outcome incidents, $16.05B, cutoff 2026-09-05, no Liquid). Non-voluntary = freezes, seizures, halts, rescues: 9.0% in the master vs 6.6% (3.5% ex-"damage averted") in the freeze brief, which uses the raw DefiLlama $17.2B denominator, drops company claims (KuCoin, Bybit) and counts the BNB 2022 halt ($429M). They add up to rounding (10.0 + 9.0 = 19.0) and no stream is wrong. Master treatment adopted as canonical because it is the only one covering all channels with one denominator.

"1 in 8" (12.5%) is a voluntary-return rate among exploits and key compromises, imputed for unresolved cases. 22.8% (150 of 659) is the share of $1M+ incidents with a documented recovery by ANY channel. The matching voluntary-only floor in the master is 78 of 659 (11.8%), consistent with 12.5%. The all-channel recovery share includes freezes, seizures and other channels in addition to voluntary returns.

8.3% (master): 95 incidents, $6.45B, gov+firm tiers, Bybit at the company-stated $78.9M, KuCoin counted at the exchange-stated $239M. 8.0% (DPRK brief): 38 curated rows, $5.56B, Bybit $42.9M, Bitget not counted. 2.8% (DPRK brief) and 3.8% (master) are the same cut without KuCoin and Munchables. 5.0% (freeze brief) is a third set: 7 named incidents 2022+, NON-voluntary channels only, no KuCoin/Munchables.
